Explanation: The Product is the Core Value Unit: the thing the Shopper ultimately comes to find, compare, choose and buy.
Shopify remains the platform Owner. Even when the Shopper never sees a Shopify storefront, Shopify can still orchestrate commerce infrastructure underneath the interaction.
Shopify’s job is to enable commerce for Merchants wherever buyers appear: online stores, physical retail, social channels and now AI conversations.
One commerce platform can potentially power transactions across many AI front ends instead of depending on Shoppers visiting one type of storefront.
If discovery moves into ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini or another Agent, Shopify no longer owns the main consumer-facing interface where the Shopper decides what to buy.

Shopify processes the commerce workflow around the order and can earn transaction-related revenue. For the Agentic Plan, Shopify says there is no monthly subscription fee; businesses pay standard payment rates when products sell through channels powered by Shopify Checkout.
Transaction Flows: ← Provider · Data — Merchants give Shopify the structured product data AI agents need, including products, variants, prices, inventory and attributes. | → Provider · Order — Shopify delivers the resulting order into the Merchant’s Admin with channel attribution and the information needed to fulfill it. | → Partner · Catalog — Shopify gives connected AI Agents structured product information through Shopify Catalog and related commerce interfaces. | ← Partner · Order — When the Shopper is ready to buy, the AI channel can send purchase intent or order information into Shopify’s commerce infrastructure.

Explanation: Shopify governs the commerce layer through product-data requirements, merchant settings, checkout rules and the standards its infrastructure exposes, but it does not fully control how an external AI Agent ranks products.
Partnerships become a growth channel: integrations with OpenAI, Microsoft and Google put Merchant products where AI users already spend time.
Shopify synchronizes product information and handles difficult commerce work around checkout, payment processing, tax, fraud and order flow.
The critical resources are Shopify Catalog and its commerce rails: the underlying systems that make checkout, payments, tax, fraud handling and orders work.
The Consumer side is Shoppers: people trying to find and buy the right product.
Shoppers want to find a product that fits what they actually need.
Instead of manually opening many stores, a Shopper can describe the need in plain language and let an AI agent narrow the options.
Traditional ecommerce often makes the Shopper do the work: search, filter, compare, reopen tabs and decide.
The Shopper contributes a query describing what they want and eventually payment when a purchase is made.
Transaction Flows: → Provider · Payment — The Shopper pays the Merchant for the purchase. Shopify Checkout or another processor may technically mediate the payment, but the economic Consumer-to-Provider relationship remains. | ← Provider · Product — The Merchant ultimately gives the Shopper the Product. Agentic commerce changes discovery and transaction orchestration, not the underlying product exchange. | → Partner · Query — The Shopper gives the AI Agent a query describing what they want and what matters. | ← Partner · Options — The AI Agent returns product options, comparisons and recommendations.

Explanation: The live buying experience is filtered by geography and channel. At the research cut-off, Shopify described purchasing across connected AI channels as available to U.S. buyers, with availability differing by platform.
The Consumer access channel can move from a merchant website to an AI chat such as ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google AI Mode or Gemini.
The Shopper asks, refines the request, compares the agent’s suggestions and chooses.
The Shopper brings purchase intent, a budget and a payment method.
Merchants are the Provider side because they supply the products that Shoppers want.
Merchants want to sell products to customers.
If products can appear in many AI conversations without a bespoke integration for every channel, Merchants can meet buyers in more places.
Merchants need to generate traffic without excessive customer-acquisition cost. If discovery increasingly begins in AI, they need to be visible there.
The Merchant provides the Product and receives the economic value of the sale.

Explanation: Participation depends on channel terms and usable product data. AI agents need current information such as price, inventory, variants and product attributes.
Merchants connect through Shopify Admin or APIs. In Admin they can manage AI-channel participation, product discovery and direct-checkout settings.
Merchants keep product data current, list what they sell and fulfill resulting orders.
Merchants contribute inventory, product information, brand assets and fulfillment capability.
AI Agents form the Partner side. They do not supply the Product, but they become essential when discovery, comparison and purchase decisions happen inside their interfaces.
AI Agents help Shoppers find relevant products, answer questions, compare options and move toward a purchase.
Useful shopping can increase usage and trust because the assistant becomes more valuable when it can help complete the Shopper’s task.
Agents need accurate live product data and dependable commerce execution: price, inventory, variants, tax, payment, fraud and order logic cannot safely be guessed.
The Agent receives the Shopper’s query and can send product requests or purchase intent into Shopify’s commerce infrastructure.

Explanation: AI channels connect through supported technical interfaces and commercial terms, and different channels can provide different discovery and checkout experiences.

Shopify Catalog provides structured product data, while Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), co-developed by Shopify and Google, gives agents and merchants a shared technical language across the commerce journey.
Agents search, rank, compare, answer questions and guide the Shopper toward a Product. Ranking logic varies by AI platform.
AI platforms contribute their own users, models, interfaces and the conversations in which demand is expressed.
